question: In an end-to-end DataOps deployment, what is the typical role of Infrastructure as Code?
options: To visualize dashboards for business users
To provision the warehouses, storage, and compute the pipelines depend on in a reproducible way
To replace the data transformation logic
To store the raw source data
explanation: IaC (for example Terraform) provisions the underlying infrastructure (warehouse, buckets, clusters) reproducibly as the foundation of a DataOps deployment.

question: What is a key benefit of an end-to-end DataOps approach that connects code, CI/CD, and orchestration?
options: It removes the need for any data testing
It guarantees data will never change
It makes the entire data lifecycle automated, versioned, tested, and observable from commit to production
It requires all work to be done manually for control
explanation: End-to-end DataOps ties together version control, automated testing, CI/CD, and orchestration so the whole pipeline lifecycle is automated, reproducible, and observable.

question: Where should data quality checks be placed in an end-to-end DataOps deployment?
options: Only after users report incorrect dashboards
Only once per year during an audit
Never, since transformations are always correct
Both in CI before merge and in the running pipeline to catch bad data at runtime
explanation: Quality checks belong in CI (to block bad changes) and in the production pipeline (to catch bad incoming data), providing defense in depth.

question: Why is observability (metrics, logs, lineage, and alerts) essential in a production DataOps deployment?
options: It enables detecting failures, freshness issues, and quality regressions so teams can respond before consumers are impacted
It replaces the need for a data warehouse
It automatically writes new transformation code
It only matters in development environments
explanation: Observability lets teams detect pipeline failures, stale data, and quality regressions early and trace issues via lineage, protecting downstream consumers.

question: Which sequence best represents a healthy end-to-end DataOps flow for a pipeline change?
options: Edit directly in production, then hope it works
Deploy first, then write tests only if something breaks
Commit to version control, run CI tests, promote the artifact through environments, deploy via automation, then monitor
Manually copy files to prod and skip version control
explanation: A healthy flow versions the change, validates it in CI, promotes the same artifact through environments via automated deployment, and monitors it in production.
